A0231.title: SROS2 & DDS-Security Deployment
A0231.definition: Enabling ROS2's SROS2 and DDS-Security (authentication, encryption, access control) to replace the default no-authentication DDS multicast configuration, preventing unauthorized robot-node access or topic injection and tampering.
A0231.description: SROS2 and DDS-Security deployment addresses the insecure default DDS configuration in ROS/ROS2, which lacks authentication, uses plaintext multicast, and allows any node to arbitrarily publish or subscribe to topics. It enables the five security SPI defined by the OMG DDS-Security specification: identity authentication, access control, data confidentiality, data integrity, and data origin authentication. SROS2 provides certificate management and PKI integration, simplifying DDS-Security deployment. Once enabled, inter-node communication requires mutual authentication, topic publish/subscribe operations are constrained by access control lists, data transmission is encrypted to prevent eavesdropping and tampering, and the DDS Discovery protocol no longer leaks all robot application information across the local area network. This measure works in conjunction with A0108 (IoT device network isolation and access control), A0118 (certificate-based device authentication), and A0146 (industrial network isolation and zone segmentation), serving as a core architecture-level defense after exploitation of ROS2 vulnerabilities such as CVE-2024-30259 (FastDDS heap overflow).
A0231.limitation: DDS-Security introduces significant performance overhead, impacting real-time control latency. Some legacy ROS nodes and cross-vendor DDS implementations exhibit poor interoperability and may not be able to enable the full set of security features. Certificate and PKI management increases deployment complexity. SROS2 implements only three of the five DDS-Security SPI, with the remaining two requiring vendor extensions.
